# Changelog

## 0.0.1

### Compatibility

* The tests are based on selected outputs generated by the original code.
  The following components are tested:
  the training data, the tree model, the CtreeX explainer in the `legacy` mode
  (meta-features, leaf matrix, leaf distance matrix, volatility and support
  sets, counterfactuals), the dialogue (`test_dialogue.py`, 390 dialogue turns)
  and (`test_nlu.py`, 169 intent mappings).
* The `spacy` backend -- now default -- reimplements the original Rasa NLU
  pipeline;
  it is trained on the 162 original and 241 new (added in 2026) examples.
  The legacy Rasa backend serves the original model unchanged via a Docker
  container.
  On held-out sentences the accuracy of the (intent, arguments) pairs rose from
  24.5% to 73.5% as reported in the
  [readme](./README.md#natural-language-understanding).
* The NLU still misunderstands some sentences;
  rephrasing or the `cmd:` syntax helps.
* The new package keeps the HTTP interfaces of the original scripts (`/led`
  commands, `/aiysay`, `/voicehat`, `/getmessage` are accepted as aliases),
  so the original scripts can still talk to the new application and vice versa.
* The original code used Google Assistant gRPC API for speech recognition,
  which Google deprecated in the meantime;
  the new implementation was ported to Google Assistant SDK but **not** tested.
* The original implementation deliberately kept spoken answers short, so with
  `implementation='fixed'` the default behaviour depends on the output channel:
  the original behaviour is kept for speech (`channel='speech'`) and the fix is
  used for chat (`channel='chat'`).

### Bug fixes and behaviour changes

The configuration file can switch between the original and new behaviour of
the code.
`implementation = "original"` reproduces the original implementation;
`implementation = "fixed"` (default) enables the fixes described below,
each of which can also be switched individually.
For example:

```toml
[dialogue]
implementation = "original"
# implementation = "fixed"    # default

[dialogue.fixes]              # individual dialogue fixes
integer_ranges = false

[dialogue.explainer_fixes]    # individual CtreeX fixes
complete_categorical_features = false
```

The `--implementation original` flag does the same for the `glassbox chat` and
`glassbox serve` commands.
In Python, this is set with `DialogueManager(implementation='original')` and
`GlassBoxModel(implementation='original')`.

#### Critical fixes (always applied)

* Debug `print`s changed to `logging`.
* `NotImplementedError` called correctly.
* Re-applying as an unknown persona no longer results in `NameError`.
* Undefined variables (e.g., `sentence` and `name`) now defined.
* Empty distance bins now give empty lists.

#### Switchable fixes (`implementation='fixed'`, the default)

##### Dialogue and intents (`DialogueFixes`, `[dialogue.fixes]`)

| Switch | Original | Fixed | Default for speech |
|--------|----------|-------|--------------------|
| `wording`             | "process you application", "had you between 100 and 500 pounds on your savings account" (missing verb), double / leading spaces, a missing comma before "your loan would be ...", lower-case sentence starts, missing full stop, housing article taken from the last option, help-text typo | corrected | fixed |
| `myself_all_features` | "tell me about myself" listed only the current account status | all features | **original** |
| `stop_when_exhausted` | after the last explanation the list silently started over | says there are no more (then starts over) | **original** |
| `integer_ranges`      | "between 954.5 and 1181.5 pounds" | "between 955 and 1181 pounds" | **original** |
| `feature_keywords`    | substring rules missed 11 of the 94 feature mentions of the NLU training data ("married", "rent", "employed", ...) and mapped "separated" to the instalment rate ("sepa**rate**d") | annotated mentions + word-boundary keywords | fixed |
| `why_reset`           | the NLU's `why_reset` entity was ignored ("restart why" only via `cmd:`) | restarts the enquiry | fixed |
| `action_restrictions` | "what can I do" ignored restrictions, although the help message suggested "Disregarding my age what can I do ...?" | "what can I do" accepts the restrictions of "why" (*despite* / *given* features, "what can I do with my X") | fixed |

##### Explainer (CtreeX, `[dialogue.explainer_fixes]`)

The explainer is [CtreeX][ctreex] version 0.0.3:
the original implementation is its `legacy` implementation;
with `implementation = "fixed"` all its fixes are enabled
(see the [CtreeX README][ctreex] for details).
Their effect on Glass-Box are as follows:

| Switch | Fix | Effect on Glass-Box |
|--------|-----|---------------------|
| `deterministic_order`               | alternatives in the order of discovery | stable answers |
| `continue_past_missing_distance`    | distances with no leaf are skipped instead of ending the search | none observed (the gaps were caused by the next issue) |
| `complete_categorical_features`     | meta-features for all the categories of a categorical feature, not only those the tree splits on | job type (A17) and housing type (A15) are split on some of their categories only; the answers of 8 personas change |
| `complete_numerical_intervals`      | both intervals of a feature split at a single threshold | none: no such feature in the tree |
| `whole_counterfactual_restrictions` | `excluded` / `included` select whole counterfactuals | none: the dialogue filters whole counterfactuals itself |
| `per_class_ranking`                 | counterfactuals merged per class | none: two classes |
| `short_thresholds`                  | shortest form of 32-bit thresholds | none: thresholds such as 954.5 |

## pre 0.0.1

* **Raspberry Pi operating system.**
  The 2018 AIY Projects image (Raspbian Stretch), configured with
  `sudo raspi-config` to enable camera and SSH;
  static Ethernet address `192.168.100.100` and Wi-Fi via `wpa_supplicant`
  (`/etc/network/interfaces.d`).

* **Software.**
  System packages: `git`, `vim`, `swig`, `scons`, `alsa-utils`, `rsync`,
  `libttspico-utils`, `ntpdate`, `zbar-tools`;
  Python 2 and 3 with `numpy`, `RPi.GPIO`, `pysocks` and `flask`.

* **Python environments.**
  A Python 3 virtualenv `py3-glassbox` (`--system-site-packages`) for the voice
  interface and the QR scanner;
  Python 2 virtualenv `py2` for the LED server, with `rpi_ws281x` built from
  source
  
  ```sh 
  git clone https://github.com/jgarff/rpi_ws281x.git
  scons
  cd python
  python setup.py install
  ```
  
  controlled by `neopixel_python` version 0.0.1.

* **Camera.**

  ```sh
  sudo modprobe bcm2835-v4l2
  zbarcam /dev/video0 --prescale=320x240 --nodisplay
  ```

* **AIY.**
  The `src/aiy` folder of `google/aiyprojects-raspbian`, commit
  `9a80eab22f2b590f56b8f4947008a4994cc8ace0` (v0.9~6) at first,
  later `e48363018e37b1fdc22d5ddc4b221db97c2cf47b` (20 April 2018),
  installed with
  
  ```sh
  pip install -r requirements.txt
  pip install google-assistant-library
  pip install --upgrade grpcio
  cd src
  python setup.py install
  sudo scripts/install-services.sh
  sudo scripts/install-alsa-config.sh
  ```

  Google Assistant (gRPC API) OAuth credentials (`client_id`, `project_id`,
  `client_secret`) in `assistant.json`.
  `/boot/config.txt` set up with

  ```ini
  dtparam=i2s=on
  dtparam=i2s-mmap
  dtoverlay=googlevoicehat-soundcard
  ```

* **Processes.**

  * The `glass-box` script handled LEDs and served `/aiysay` at `192.168.1.252`
    or `192.168.1.123` on port 5000 with Python 2.

  * The `voice_interface` and `qr_scanner` scripts run with Python 3 on the
    Raspberry Pi.

  * Rasa NLU was run on a laptop at `192.168.1.32`.

  * The `text_interface` script, which was a fork of `sohelamin/chatbot` run
    with `gunicorn --bind 0.0.0.0:5000 wsgi`, provided the chat server
    (the brain / AIML chatbot was not used).

  * The counterfactual explainer became [CtreeX][ctreex] version 0.0.3.

  * Data and model components moved to [MLaaS][mlaas] version 0.0.1.

  * The LED drivers became [neopixel-python][neopixel] version 0.0.1.

[ctreex]: https://github.com/So-Cool/ctreex
[mlaas]: https://github.com/So-Cool/MLaaS
[neopixel]: https://github.com/So-Cool/neopixel-python
